newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends up on expiry-tied short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends up on expiry-tied short covering.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended with strong gains Friday on short covering ahead of the May crude contract expiry on Tuesday, pushing up prices of gasoline and heating oil in the rally.
"I think what you have is a good old fashioned short squeeze here," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston.
May crude ended 49 cents higher at $19.91 a barrel. May heating oil ended 0.68 cent higher at 54.68 cents a gallon while May gasoline ended up 0.79 cent at 61.49 cents a gallon.
According to the most recent CFTC Futures Commitment of Traders report, speculators had set a large amount of short positions in crude, betting crude's price would fall.
Indeed, since January, crude prices have dropped more than seven dollars a barrel on a surplus in domestic crude.

But, Saucer said refiner demand for crude picks up in May in order to make gasoline ahead of the summer driving season, pushing up crude prices and forcing traders to close their bet of a decline in crude.

Moreover, after facing a crude surfeit for months, refiners may be faced with tightened crude supply after IPL Energy Inc lost one million barrels per day of throughput on its pipeline system for several days earlier this month, Saucer said.

IPL had to shut several lines on its pipeline system after bad weather in Minnesota knocked out three pumping stations. The huge system runs from Western Canada through the U.S. Midwest to Eastern Canada.

"The IPL incident could very well be felt, especially in the Midcontinent where they need crude," said Saucer. Tighter crude supplies would make it difficult for traders with short positions who end up having to deliver crude if they do not settle their positions with cash.
The IPL had to shut four pipelines on the system again Friday following a minor oil spill, but the shutdown was expected to be shortlived.

Also acting as incentive for covering a short position Friday was talk by traders that ARCO is delivering Nigerian Bonny Light crude against the NYMEX May contract instead of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) at Cushing, Oklahoma, tightening the availability of WTI.
ARCO officials were not immediately available to comment.
As owner of the oil installations at Cushing, ARCO is seen in a strategic position to make such a delivery, dealers said.
